Mr. Shobhit Saharia, learned counsel for the appellant.
Mr. Ghanshyam Joshi and Mr. H.M. Raturi, learned counsel for the private respondents.
Mr. I.P. Kohli, learned Standing Counsel for the State.

Respondent nos.1/1/, 1/2 and 1/3 have placed on record, the order of 11.09.2021, which is said to have been passed by the Permanent Lok Adalat, observing therein, that certain settlement has been arrived at in the matter in question.
As such, no adjudication is required to be made in this First Appeal, as it has been preferred under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act.

The issue about the propriety of order of 11.09.2021, was in debate on number of earlier occasions,
on the ground, that the appellant herein is not a signatory to the compromise.
As such, it was contended by the learned counsel for the appellant, that they are not bound by the order of 11.09.2021.
On the contrary, learned counsel for the respondents argues that since the land was acquired by the State, the THDC was not required to be heard by the Lok Adalat.

This contention raised by the respondents may not be correct, in the light of the judgment of U.P.
Awas Evam Vikas Parishad Vs. Gyan Devi and Others, as reported in (1995) 2 SCC 326 and Neyvely Lignite Corporation Ltd. Vs. Special Tehsildar (Land Acquisition) Neyvely and Others, as reported in (1995) 1 SCC 221, where it has been settled that the beneficiary of an acquisition has had to be made as a party in a proceedings determining quantification of compensation.
